fragments.plaintext: Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone:
meta.com/thefutureisforeveryone
Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.

caption.text:
Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone: meta.com/thefutureisforeveryone 

Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.

fragments.plaintext:
The reality is:

- People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask, so labs have a strong natural incentive to make their models more aligned.

There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.

- People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask, so labs have a strong natural incentive to make their models more aligned.

There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.

fragments.plaintext:
- Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this as well. 

Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us. I'm proud of the security foundations we've built.

Other labs can just do this too. In general, it would be helpful for there to be a larger and more diverse ecosystem of evaluators.

fragments.plaintext: Introducing
@Muse

, the personal agent that understands your goals and works 24/7 to get things done for you.

Your Muse gets its own private computer in the cloud to do work for you. We've built new technology so the Muse Secure VM keeps your content safe. 

We want everyone to have access to personal superintelligence, so we're providing Muse for free for up to 100 million tokens per week.

fragments.plaintext: Muse Voice Transcribe is MSL's first real-time audio perception model -- rolling out today. SOTA in streaming speech-to-text, it handles speaker diarization, and endpointing natively in a single model.

caption.text: Muse Voice Transcribe is MSL's first real-time audio perception model -- rolling out today. SOTA in streaming speech-to-text, it handles speaker diarization, and endpointing natively in a single model.

fragments.plaintext: The model decides when to listen. It waits a little longer on hard words and commits faster on easy ones, using adaptive delay to predict each token and increase accuracy. With adaptive delay, the model is near the pareto front on speed-accuracy tradeoff.

caption.text: The model decides when to listen. It waits a little longer on hard words and commits faster on easy ones, using adaptive delay to predict each token and increase accuracy. With adaptive delay, the model is near the pareto front on speed-accuracy tradeoff.

fragments.plaintext: It holds up on messy, real audio too -- trained across 70+ languages (with 25 validated at launch), handles mid-sentence code-switching, and manages hour-long sessions with 20+ speakers. You can bias it toward names and domain terms as well.

fragments.plaintext: Sessions can share context with inter-session messaging. When two are working on things that affect each other, they share state directly, instead of the developer copying it over manually.

fragments.plaintext: Workflows can break out a task across multiple focused agents, carry the intermediate work between stages, and return one result at the end. Good for engineering work that's too complex for a single agent.
